plain: Speaking in a dodging, misleading way to avoid the truth

webster.text: A shuffling or quibbling to evade the truth or the disclosure of truth; the practice of some trick for evading what is just or honorable; a deviation from the plain path of truth and fair dealing.

more.text: A secret abuse in the exercise of a public office or commission.

example.quote: This, he said, would admit of no prevarication.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, Massachusetts Convention, Mr. BISHOP, January 16, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
